title: एकाशीत्यधिकशततमोऽध्यायः

summary.en: Yudhishthira asks why he suffers though righteous. Markandeya explains how beings fare according to their deeds, in this world and the next, and assures the Pandavas that by their own good actions they will reach heaven.
summary.kn: ಧರ್ಮಿಷ್ಠನಾದರೂ ತಾನೇಕೆ ನರಳುತ್ತಿದ್ದೇನೆ ಎಂದು ಯುಧಿಷ್ಠಿರನು ಕೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಜೀವಿಗಳು ಈ ಲೋಕ ಪರಲೋಕಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕರ್ಮಾನುಸಾರ ಫಲ ಪಡೆಯುವುದನ್ನು ವಿವರಿಸಿ, ತಮ್ಮ ಸತ್ಕರ್ಮಗಳಿಂದ ಸ್ವರ್ಗ ಸೇರುವಿರಿ ಎಂದು ಮಾರ್ಕಂಡೇಯರು ಭರವಸೆ ನೀಡುತ್ತಾರೆ.
summary.hi: युधिष्ठिर पूछते हैं कि धर्मात्मा होकर भी वे क्यों दुःख पाते हैं। मार्कण्डेय समझाते हैं कि प्राणी इस लोक और परलोक में अपने कर्मों के अनुसार फल पाते हैं, और पाण्डवों को आश्वासन देते हैं कि वे अपने शुभ कर्मों से स्वर्ग पाएँगे।
summary.te: ధర్మాత్ముడైనా తాను ఎందుకు బాధపడుతున్నానని యుధిష్ఠిరుడు అడుగుతాడు. జీవులు ఈ లోకంలో, పరలోకంలో కర్మానుసారం ఫలం పొందుతారని మార్కండేయుడు వివరించి, తమ సత్కర్మలతో స్వర్గం చేరుతారని పాండవులకు భరోసా ఇస్తాడు.
summary.ta: அறவோனாக இருந்தும் தாம் ஏன் துன்புறுகிறோம் என்று யுதிஷ்டிரர் கேட்கிறார். உயிர்கள் இம்மையிலும் மறுமையிலும் தம் வினைகளுக்கேற்பப் பலன் பெறுவதை மார்க்கண்டேயர் விளக்கி, தம் நற்செயல்களால் ஸ்வர்க்கம் அடைவீர்கள் என்று பாண்டவர்களுக்கு உறுதியளிக்கிறார்.
summary.ml: താൻ നീതിമാനായിട്ടും എന്തുകൊണ്ട് കഷ്ടപ്പെടുന്നുവെന്ന് യുധിഷ്ഠിരൻ ചോദിക്കുന്നു. ഈ ലോകത്തും പരലോകത്തും ജീവികൾ അവരവരുടെ കർമ്മഫലം എങ്ങനെ അനുഭവിക്കുന്നുവെന്ന് മാർക്കണ്ഡേയൻ വിശദീകരിക്കുന്നു; സ്വന്തം സൽകർമ്മങ്ങളാൽ പാണ്ഡവർ സ്വർഗ്ഗത്തിലെത്തുമെന്ന് അദ്ദേഹം ഉറപ്പു നൽകുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 3.181; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Apr 11 2022

verses.text: वैशंपायन उवाच

meaning.en: Vaishampayana said:

verses.text:
तं विवक्षन्तमालक्ष्य कुरुराजो महामुनिम् ।
कथासंजननार्थाय चोदयामास पाण्डवः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing the great sage wishing to speak, the Pandava king of the Kurus urged him on, to start the story.

verses.text:
भवान्दैवतदैत्यानामृषीणां च महात्मनाम् ।
राजर्षीणां च सर्वेषां चरितज्ञः सनातनः ॥

meaning.en: "You are the eternal knower of the deeds of gods, daityas, great-souled sages and all royal sages.

verses.text:
सेव्यश्चोपासितव्यश्च मतो नः काङ्क्षितश्चिरम् ।
अयं च देवकीपुत्रः प्राप्तोऽस्मानवलोककः ॥

meaning.en: We have long thought you worthy of service and attendance, and desired you; and this son of Devaki has come to see us.

verses.text:
भवत्येव हि मे बुद्धिर्दृष्ट्वात्मानं सुखाच्च्युतम् ।
धार्तराष्ट्रांश्च दुर्वृत्तानृध्यतः प्रेक्ष्य सर्वशः ॥

meaning.en: A thought comes to me, seeing myself fallen from happiness and seeing Dhritarashtra's evil-conducting sons prospering everywhere.

verses.text:
कर्मणः पुरुषः कर्ता शुभस्याप्यशुभस्य च ।
स्वफलं तदुपाश्नाति कथं कर्ता स्विदीश्वरः ॥

meaning.en: A man is the doer of a deed, good or bad, and gets its fruit himself. How then is the Lord the doer?

verses.text:
अथ वा सुखदुःखेषु नृणां ब्रह्मविदां वर ।
इह वा कृतमन्वेति परदेहेऽथ वा पुनः ॥

meaning.en: Or, best of the knowers of Brahman, does what a man does here follow him in happiness and sorrow, in another body or elsewhere?

verses.text:
देही च देहं संत्यज्य मृग्यमाणः शुभाशुभैः ।
कथं संयुज्यते प्रेत्य इह वा द्विजसत्तम ॥

meaning.en: And the embodied one, leaving the body, sought out by his good and bad deeds, how is he joined to them after death, or here, best of brahmins?

verses.text:
ऐहलौकिकमेवैतदुताहो पारलौकिकम् ।
क्व च कर्माणि तिष्ठन्ति जन्तोः प्रेतस्य भार्गव ॥

meaning.en: Is this only for this world, or for the next? And where do deeds of a creature who has died abide, descendant of Bhrigu?"

verses.text: मार्कण्डेय उवाच

meaning.en: Markandeya said:

verses.text:
त्वद्युक्तोऽयमनुप्रश्नो यथावद्वदतां वर ।
विदितं वेदितव्यं ते स्थित्यर्थमनुपृच्छसि ॥

meaning.en: This question is well put by you, best of speakers. You know what is to be known; you ask for the sake of the settled truth.

verses.text:
अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि तदिहैकमनाः शृणु ।
यथेहामुत्र च नरः सुखदुःखमुपाश्नुते ॥

meaning.en: On this I will explain to you; listen here with one mind, how a man gets pleasure and pain here and hereafter.

verses.text:
निर्मलानि शरीराणि विशुद्धानि शरीरिणाम् ।
ससर्ज धर्मतन्त्राणि पूर्वोत्पन्नः प्रजापतिः ॥

meaning.en: In the beginning, the Lord of creatures, born first, made the bodies of embodied beings pure and spotless, subject to dharma.

verses.text:
अमोघबलसंकल्पाः सुव्रताः सत्यवादिनः ।
ब्रह्मभूता नराः पुण्याः पुराणाः कुरुनन्दन ॥

meaning.en: Those men, delight of the Kurus, were pure, ancient, of unfailing strength and will, keepers of good vows, truthful, and like Brahman.

verses.text:
सर्वे देवैः समायान्ति स्वच्छन्देन नभस्तलम् ।
ततश्च पुनरायान्ति सर्वे स्वच्छन्दचारिणः ॥

meaning.en: All of them went with the gods to the sky at will, and then all came back again, going as they pleased.

verses.text:
स्वच्छन्दमरणाश्चासन्नराः स्वच्छन्दजीविनः ।
अल्पबाधा निरातङ्का सिद्धार्था निरुपद्रवाः ॥

meaning.en: They died at will and lived at will, with few troubles, without fear, fulfilled in their aims and free from calamity.

verses.text:
द्रष्टारो देवसंघानामृषीणां च महात्मनाम् ।
प्रत्यक्षाः सर्वधर्माणां दान्ता विगतमत्सराः ॥

meaning.en: They were seers of the hosts of gods and of the great-souled sages, direct witnesses of all dharmas, self-controlled and free from envy.

verses.text:
आसन्वर्षसहस्राणि तथा पुत्रसहस्रिणः ।
ततः कालान्तरेऽन्यस्मिन्पृथिवीतलचारिणः ॥

meaning.en: They lived thousands of years and had thousands of sons. Then, in another age, they came to walk on the surface of the earth.

verses.text:
कामक्रोधाभिभूतास्ते मायाव्याजोपजीविनः ।
लोभमोहाभिभूताश्च त्यक्ता देवैस्ततो नराः ॥

meaning.en: Overcome by desire and anger, living by sorcery and deceit, overcome by greed and delusion, those men were abandoned by the gods.

verses.text:
अशुभैः कर्मभिः पापास्तिर्यङ्नरकगामिनः ।
संसारेषु विचित्रेषु पच्यमानाः पुनः पुनः ॥

meaning.en: Sinners through evil deeds, they went to animal births and hells, cooked again and again in the varied cycles of rebirth.

verses.text:
मोघेष्टा मोघसंकल्पा मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः ।
सर्वातिशङ्किनश्चैव संवृत्ताः क्लेशभागिनः ।
अशुभैः कर्मभिश्चापि प्रायशः परिचिह्निताः ॥

meaning.en: With vain rites, vain intentions and vain knowledge, senseless, suspecting everything, they became sharers of suffering, usually marked by their evil deeds.

verses.text:
दौष्कुल्या व्याधिबहुला दुरात्मानोऽप्रतापिनः ।
भवन्त्यल्पायुषः पापा रौद्रकर्मफलोदयाः ।
नाथन्तः सर्वकामानां नास्तिका भिन्नसेतवः ॥

meaning.en: They were born of bad families, full of disease, wicked-minded, without splendor, short-lived, wrongdoers with the results of cruel deeds arising, lacking all desires, unbelievers, breakers of the bounds.

verses.text:
जन्तोः प्रेतस्य कौन्तेय गतिः स्वैरिह कर्मभिः ।
प्राज्ञस्य हीनबुद्धेश्च कर्मकोशः क्व तिष्ठति ॥

meaning.en: For a creature who has died, Kunti's son, the course is by his own deeds here. Where does the store of deeds stay, for the wise and for the dull-minded alike?

verses.text:
क्वस्थस्तत्समुपाश्नाति सुकृतं यदि वेतरत् ।
इति ते दर्शनं यच्च तत्राप्यनुनयं शृणु ॥

meaning.en: And where abiding does one enjoy it, whether it is good or otherwise? As for this view of yours, hear my reply to it too.

verses.text:
अयमादिशरीरेण देवसृष्टेन मानवः ।
शुभानामशुभानां च कुरुते संचयं महत् ॥

meaning.en: This man, with the first body made by the gods, makes a great accumulation of good and bad deeds.

verses.text:
आयुषोऽन्ते प्रहायेदं क्षीणप्रायं कलेवरम् ।
संभवत्येव युगपद्योनौ नास्त्यन्तराभवः ॥

meaning.en: At the end of his life, leaving this nearly spent body, he is at once born in a womb; there is no state in between.

verses.text:
तत्रास्य स्वकृतं कर्म छायेवानुगतं सदा ।
फलत्यथ सुखार्हो वा दुःखार्हो वापि जायते ॥

meaning.en: There his own deed follows him always like a shadow and bears fruit, and he is born fit for happiness or fit for pain.

verses.text:
कृतान्तविधिसंयुक्तः स जन्तुर्लक्षणैः शुभैः ।
अशुभैर्वा निरादानो लक्ष्यते ज्ञानदृष्टिभिः ॥

meaning.en: Bound by the order of fate, that creature, without support, is seen by those with the eyes of knowledge by auspicious or inauspicious signs.

verses.text:
एषा तावदबुद्धीनां गतिरुक्ता युधिष्ठिर ।
अतः परं ज्ञानवतां निबोध गतिमुत्तमाम् ॥

meaning.en: This, Yudhishthira, is stated as the course of the unwise. Now hear the highest course of those who have knowledge.

verses.text:
मनुष्यास्तप्ततपसः सर्वागमपरायणाः ।
स्थिरव्रताः सत्यपरा गुरुशुश्रूषणे रताः ॥

meaning.en: Men who have practiced austerity, devoted to all the scriptures, firm in vows, intent on truth and happy to serve their teachers,

verses.text:
सुशीलाः शुक्लजातीयाः क्षान्ता दान्ताः सुतेजसः ।
शुभयोन्यन्तरगताः प्रायशः शुभलक्षणाः ॥

meaning.en: of good conduct, of pure birth, patient, self-controlled and very radiant, born into good wombs, mostly with good marks,

verses.text:
जितेन्द्रियत्वाद्वशिनः शुक्लत्वान्मन्दरोगिणः ।
अल्पबाधपरित्रासाद्भवन्ति निरुपद्रवाः ॥

meaning.en: through control of the senses they are masters, through purity they are little diseased, and through little trouble and fear they are free from calamity.

verses.text:
च्यवन्तं जायमानं च गर्भस्थं चैव सर्वशः ।
स्वमात्मानं परं चैव बुध्यन्ते ज्ञानचक्षुषः ।
कर्मभूमिमिमां प्राप्य पुनर्यान्ति सुरालयम् ॥

meaning.en: With the eye of knowledge they understand themselves and others in all states, as one falls, is being born, and is in the womb; and having reached this field of action, they go again to the home of the gods.

verses.text:
किंचिद्दैवाद्धठात्किंचित्किंचिदेव स्वकर्मभिः ।
प्राप्नुवन्ति नरा राजन्मा तेऽस्त्वन्या विचारणा ॥

meaning.en: Men obtain something by fate, something by force and something by their own deeds, O king. Let you have no other thought about it.

verses.text:
इमामत्रोपमां चापि निबोध वदतां वर ।
मनुष्यलोके यच्छ्रेयः परं मन्ये युधिष्ठिर ॥

meaning.en: Hear also this comparison, best of speakers, about what I consider the highest good in the human world, Yudhishthira.

verses.text:
इह वैकस्य नामुत्र अमुत्रैकस्य नो इह ।
इह चामुत्र चैकस्य नामुत्रैकस्य नो इह ॥

meaning.en: For one there is this world and not the next; for another the next and not this; for another both this and the next; for another neither this nor the next.

verses.text:
धनानि येषां विपुलानि सन्ति
नित्यं रमन्ते सुविभूषिताङ्गाः ।
तेषामयं शत्रुवरघ्न लोको
नासौ सदा देहसुखे रतानाम् ॥

meaning.en: Those who have great wealth and always enjoy themselves with well-adorned bodies have this world, slayer of the best foes, but not the other, being always devoted to bodily pleasure.

verses.text:
ये योगयुक्तास्तपसि प्रसक्ताः
स्वाध्यायशीला जरयन्ति देहान् ।
जितेन्द्रिया भूतहिते निविष्टा-
स्तेषामसौ नायमरिघ्न लोकः ॥

meaning.en: Those who are united with yoga, given to austerity, devoted to study, who wear down their bodies, who have conquered their senses and are intent on the good of beings, have the other world and not this, slayer of enemies.

verses.text:
ये धर्ममेव प्रथमं चरन्ति
धर्मेण लब्ध्वा च धनानि काले ।
दारानवाप्य क्रतुभिर्यजन्ते
तेषामयं चैव परश्च लोकः ॥

meaning.en: Those who practice dharma first and, having gained wealth by dharma at the right time and taken wives, sacrifice with rites, have both this world and the other.

verses.text:
ये नैव विद्यां न तपो न दानं
न चापि मूढाः प्रजने यतन्ते ।
न चाधिगच्छन्ति सुखान्यभाग्या-
स्तेषामयं चैव परश्च नास्ति ॥

meaning.en: Those fools who strive for neither learning nor austerity nor giving, nor even for offspring, and who do not find happiness, the unfortunate, have neither this world nor the other.

verses.text:
सर्वे भवन्तस्त्वतिवीर्यसत्त्वा
दिव्यौजसः संहननोपपन्नाः ।
लोकादमुष्मादवनिं प्रपन्नाः
स्वधीतविद्याः सुरकार्यहेतोः ॥

meaning.en: All of you are of surpassing strength and spirit, of divine energy and well-built, who came from that world to earth, having studied well, for the sake of the gods' work.

verses.text:
कृत्वैव कर्माणि महान्ति शूरा-
स्तपोदमाचारविहारशीलाः ।
देवानृषीन्प्रेतगणांश्च सर्वा-
न्संतर्पयित्वा विधिना परेण ॥

meaning.en: Having done great deeds, as heroes devoted to austerity, self-control, right conduct and recreation, and having satisfied gods, sages and all the ancestors by the highest rite,

verses.text:
स्वर्गं परं पुण्यकृतां निवासं
क्रमेण संप्राप्स्यथ कर्मभिः स्वैः ।
मा भूद्विशङ्का तव कौरवेन्द्र
दृष्ट्वात्मनः क्लेशमिमं सुखार्ह ॥

meaning.en: you will in due order reach by your own deeds the highest heaven, the abode of those who have done good. Let there be no doubt, O king of the Kurus, on seeing this affliction of yours who deserve happiness.
